summary: The note describes the Daihatsu Charmant, a subcompact sedan built by Japanese automaker Daihatsu and based on the Toyota Corolla. It was later replaced by the Daihatsu Applause. The Charmant began as a spin-off of the 1970s Toyota Corolla, with model changes following the Corolla's, and all versions used Toyota inline-four engines of 1.2 to 1.6 litres.
one_line: The Daihatsu Charmant was a Toyota Corolla-based subcompact sedan from Daihatsu, replaced by the Applause.
key_facts: The Daihatsu Charmant is a subcompact sedan built by Daihatsu of Japan.
The Daihatsu Charmant is based on the Toyota Corolla.
The Daihatsu Charmant was replaced by the Daihatsu Applause.
The Daihatsu Charmant was originally a spin-off of the Toyota Corolla of the 1970s.
Model changes to the Daihatsu Charmant paralleled those of the Toyota Corolla.
All Daihatsu Charmant models were fitted with Toyota inline-four engines.
Daihatsu Charmant engines ranged from 1.2 litres to 1.6 litres.
The word "charmant" is French for charming.
